newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Alpha Credit Bank yesterday shouldered the burdens of a leader and created new conditions and strong pressure on other banks by slashing its prime rate by 225 basis points to 12.50 percent to attract new customers and carve out a stake in the drachma lending market.

--The de-escalation of inflation continues apace creating hope that the rate will reach the government's goal of 4.5 percent by the end of the year. For the first time, the wholesale price index in March recorded no rise, stabilised at February levels.

--The ski piste of Parnassos will pass into the hands of the private sector - as well the Kamena Vourla camping grounds and five spas in the Fthiotidos prefecture. The new managers will be called on to make signficant investments.

--Reports say the finance ministry is receiving pressure from ministry officials and businessmen to shelve a new programme that is expected to bring in extra revenues of 200 billion drachmas per year through tax checks on the authenticity of transaction documents.

--Yesterday's move by the Alpha Credit Bank comes to confirm latest reports that major changes in interest rates are on the horizon. The National Bank's response to the latest round of rate cut set off by Alpha Credit is expected soon.
--There's only spitting distance between yesterday's general price index levels and the 1,600 barrier.
--The development ministry is to announce the state procurements programme within the next few days: sources say the budget for the programme will be down by about 350 billion drachmas.
--Alpha Credit said yesterday it expected profits to be up by at least 30 percent in 1997, as it announced a new round of rate cuts yesterday.
--The rise of the yen on international money markets is causing concern among those with forex loans in yen.
--Apart from Alpha Credit's move to cut rates, the Bank of Greece yesterday decided to reduce its Lombard, rediscount and overdue payment rates by one percent.
--Unions are divided on how to deal with the radical changes wanted by the government to the job market, due to be discussed at social dialogue beginning tomorrow.

--European Union economy and finance ministers meeting in Brussels yesterday stressed Greece had to do something about its excessive fiscal deficit so that it can participate in economic and monetary union.
